inline.s: Subhuti, if a bodhisattva gives while his mind abides in a dharma, it is as if a man entered into darkness and saw nothing. If a bodhisattva gives while his mind does not abide in a dharma, it is as if a man with eyes, bright with the sunlight, saw all kinds of forms.

Subhuti, in the age to come, if good men and good women are able to receive, hold, and recite this sutra, then the Tathagata, with his Buddha-wisdom, will know and see such persons, and they will all achieve immeasurable and boundless merit.

blocks.text: Part Fifteen: The Merit of Upholding the Sutra

inline.s: Subhuti, if good men and good women gave up their bodies as many as the sands of the Ganges in the morning, again gave up their bodies as many as the sands of the Ganges at midday, and again gave up their bodies as many as the sands of the Ganges in the evening; and if in this manner, for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of kotis of aeons, they gave up their bodies; and if another person, hearing this sutra, did not reject it with his faith, his merit would surpass theirs. How much more so the merit of one who copies it, receives and holds it, recites it, and expounds it for others.

Subhuti, to sum up, this sutra possesses merit that is inconceivable, incommensurable, and boundless. The Tathagata has spoken it for those who set forth in the Great Vehicle, for those who set forth in the Supreme Vehicle.

If a person is able to receive, hold, and recite it, and broadly expound it for others, the Tathagata will know such a person and see him, and he will achieve merit that is immeasurable, incommensurable, boundless, and inconceivable. Such a person thus bears on his shoulders the Tathagata’s anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.
Why? Subhuti, those who delight in lesser dharmas, being attached to the view of self, person, being, and lifespan, are unable to hear, receive, and recite this sutra, nor to expound it for others.

Subhuti, wherever this sutra is found, all the worlds, their devas, humans, and asuras, should make offerings. Know that this place is a stupa. All should respectfully worship, circumambulate, and scatter flowers and incense upon it.

Furthermore, Subhuti, if good men and good women receive, hold, and recite this sutra, yet are despised by others, it is because the karmic offenses of their former lives should have cast them into the evil paths. But because in this present life they are despised, the karmic offenses of their former lives are thereby dissolved, and they shall attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

Subhuti, I recall that in the past, in immeasurable asamkhyeya aeons, before Dipankara Buddha, I met and respectfully served and offered to eighty-four hundred thousand myriads of nayutas of Buddhas, without missing a single one. If another person, in the last age, is able to receive, hold, and recite this sutra, the merit he obtains will not be one-hundredth, not one-thousandth, not one-myriadth of it — nor can number or simile ever reach it.

Subhuti, if good men and good women, in the last age, receive, hold, and recite this sutra, and I were to tell in full of the merit they obtain, some who heard it would be driven mad, their minds confused, and would be full of doubt and disbelief. Subhuti, know that the meaning of this sutra is inconceivable, and its retribution likewise is inconceivable.

At that time Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, when good men and good women resolve their minds upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, how should they abide? How should they subdue their minds?

The Buddha told Subhuti: A good man or good woman who resolves his mind upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi should give rise to this mind: I shall lead all living beings to extinction; and when all living beings are led to extinction, in truth there is no living being who is led to extinction.
Why is this? Subhuti, in truth there is no dharma by which a mind is resolved upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

Subhuti, what do you think? When the Tathagata was with Dipankara Buddha, did he attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi through any dharma? No, World-Honored One. As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has spoken, the Buddha, with Dipankara Buddha, attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi through no dharma.

The Buddha said: Even so, even so. Subhuti, in truth there is no dharma by which the Tathagata attains anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. Subhuti, if there were a dharma by which the Tathagata attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, then Dipankara Buddha would not have bestowed upon me the prophecy: ‘In a future life you shall become a Buddha, named Shakyamuni.’ Because in truth there is no dharma by which anuttara-samyak-sambodhi is attained, therefore Dipankara Buddha bestowed upon me the prophecy, saying: ‘In a life to come you shall become a Buddha, named Shakyamuni.’
Why? ‘Tathagata’ means that all dharmas are thus, the principle of thusness.

If someone says the Tathagata attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, Subhuti, in truth there is no dharma by which the Buddha attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. Subhuti, the anuttara-samyak-sambodhi attained by the Tathagata is in it neither real nor unreal.
Therefore the Tathagata says that all dharmas are Buddha-dharmas. Subhuti, what is called all dharmas is not all dharmas; therefore it is called all dharmas.

Subhuti, it is like a person whose body is great and long. Subhuti said: World-Honored One, what the Tathagata speaks of as the great and long body is not the great body; therefore it is called the great body.

Subhuti, a bodhisattva is also thus. If he says, ‘I shall lead immeasurable living beings to extinction,’ he is not called a bodhisattva. Why? Subhuti, in truth there is no dharma called bodhisattva. Therefore the Buddha says that all dharmas are without self, without person, without being, without lifespan.

Subhuti, if a bodhisattva says, ‘I shall adorn the Buddha-land,’ he is not called a bodhisattva. Why? What the Tathagata speaks of as adorning the Buddha-land is not an adornment; therefore it is called an adornment. Subhuti, a bodhisattva who is fully versed in the dharma of no-self is called by the Tathagata a true bodhisattva.

blocks.text: Part Eighteen: One Body, One Perception

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the fleshly eye? Even so, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the fleshly eye.
Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the heavenly eye? Even so, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the heavenly eye.
Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the eye of wisdom? Even so, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the eye of wisdom.
Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the eye of the Dharma? Even so, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the eye of the Dharma.
Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the Buddha eye? Even so, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the Buddha eye.
Subhuti, what do you think? Of all the sands in the Ganges, does the Buddha say they are sands? Even so, World-Honored One, the Tathagata says they are sands.

Subhuti, what do you think? If there were Ganges rivers for each of the sands in one Ganges, and there were Buddha-worlds for all the sands of all those Ganges rivers, would they be many? Very many, World-Honored One. The Buddha told Subhuti: In all those lands, all the living beings, with their manifold minds, the Tathagata knows them all.
Why? Because the Tathagata speaks of all minds as not minds; therefore they are called minds.
How is this? Subhuti, the past mind is unattainable, the present mind is unattainable, and the future mind is unattainable.

blocks.text: Part Nineteen: Universal Transformation of the Dharma Realm

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? If a person filled the three thousand great thousand worlds with the seven treasures and used them for giving, would this person, by this cause, gain much merit? Even so, World-Honored One, this person, by this cause, would gain very much merit.
Subhuti, if merit were real, the Tathagata would not speak of gaining much merit; because merit is non-existent, the Tathagata says he gains much merit.

blocks.text: Part Twenty: Leaving Form and Marks

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? Can the Buddha be seen as having a complete form body? No, World-Honored One. The Tathagata should not be seen as a complete form body. Why? What the Tathagata speaks of as a complete form body is not a complete form body; therefore it is called a complete form body.

Subhuti, what do you think? Can the Tathagata be seen as complete in all marks? No, World-Honored One. The Tathagata should not be seen as complete in all marks. Why? What the Tathagata speaks of as complete in all marks is not complete; therefore it is called complete in all marks.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-one: What Is Not Spoken Yet Is Spoken

inline.s: Subhuti, do not say that the Tathagata thinks, ‘I shall expound a dharma.’ Do not think thus. Why? If a person says the Tathagata has expounded a dharma, he slanders the Buddha, because he cannot understand what I have spoken. Subhuti, one who expounds the dharma has no dharma to expound; therefore he is called an expounder of the dharma.
At that time the wise Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, will there be living beings in a future age who, hearing this Dharma, give rise to faith?

The Buddha said: Subhuti, they are neither living beings nor not-living-beings. Why? Subhuti, ‘living beings, living beings’ — the Tathagata speaks of them as not living beings; therefore they are called living beings.
Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, has the Buddha’s attainment of anuttara-samyak-sambodhi been no attainment?
The Buddha said: Even so, even so. Subhuti, in anuttara-samyak-sambodhi I have not obtained even the slightest dharma; therefore it is called anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-three: Purifying the Mind, Practicing Good

inline.s: Furthermore, Subhuti, this Dharma is equal, with neither high nor low; this is called anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. With no self, no person, no being, no lifespan, and by cultivating all good dharmas, one attains anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.
Subhuti, what are called good dharmas — the Tathagata speaks of them as not good dharmas; therefore they are called good dharmas.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-four: Incomparable Merit and Wisdom

inline.s: Subhuti, if in the three thousand great thousand worlds there were collections of the seven treasures as numerous as all the kings of mountains, Mount Sumeru, and if a person used them for giving; and if another person held, recited, and expounded for others this Prajnaparamita sutra, even a four-line gatha — the former merit would not amount to one-hundredth, one-thousandth, one-hundred-thousandth, one-myriadth of it; nor can number or simile ever reach it.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-five: Transformation With Nothing to Transform

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? You should not say that the Tathagata thinks, ‘I shall deliver living beings.’

Subhuti, do not think thus. Why? In truth there are no living beings whom the Tathagata delivers. If there were living beings the Tathagata delivered, then the Tathagata would have self, person, being, and lifespan.
Subhuti, what the Tathagata speaks of as self is not self; yet ordinary people think there is a self.
Subhuti, ordinary people — the Tathagata speaks of them as not ordinary people; therefore they are called ordinary people.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-six: The Dharma Body Has No Marks

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? Can the Tathagata be perceived by means of the thirty-two marks? Subhuti said: Even so, even so, the Tathagata is perceived by means of the thirty-two marks.

The Buddha said: Subhuti, if the Tathagata is perceived by means of the thirty-two marks, then a wheel-turning sage king is the Tathagata. Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, as I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has spoken, the Tathagata should not be perceived by means of the thirty-two marks.
At that time the World-Honored One spoke this verse:
If one sees me by means of form, or if one seeks me by means of sound,
That person treads a heterodox path and cannot see the Tathagata.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-seven: Neither Annihilated nor Extinguished

inline.s: Subhuti, if you think the Tathagata attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi because of his complete marks, Subhuti, do not think that the Tathagata attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi because of his complete marks.

Subhuti, if you think that one who resolves his mind upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi speaks of all dharmas as annihilated, do not think thus. Why? One who resolves his mind upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi does not speak of the mark of annihilation.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-eight: Neither Receiving nor Coveting

inline.s: Subhuti, if a bodhisattva filled worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges with the seven treasures and used them for giving; and if another person knew that all dharmas are without self and attained the patience of non-arising, this bodhisattva’s merit would surpass the former bodhisattva’s merit. Why? Subhuti, because the bodhisattvas do not receive merit.

Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, how is it that a bodhisattva does not receive merit? Subhuti, the merit a bodhisattva produces should not be clung to; therefore it is said that he does not receive merit.

Subhuti, if a person says the Tathagata comes, or goes, or sits, or lies down, that person does not understand what I have spoken. Why? ‘Tathagata’ means one who comes from nowhere and goes nowhere; therefore he is called the Tathagata.

blocks.text: Part Thirty: The Single Unified Form

inline.s: Subhuti, if good men and good women ground the three thousand great thousand worlds into particles of dust, what do you think? Would this mass of particles be many? Subhuti said: Very many, World-Honored One. Why? Because if this mass of particles truly existed, the Buddha would not have spoken of a mass of particles. How is this? What the Buddha speaks of as a mass of particles is not a mass of particles; therefore it is called a mass of particles.

World-Honored One, what the Tathagata speaks of as the three thousand great thousand worlds is not a world; therefore it is called a world. Why? If a world truly existed, it would be a union of a single mass of particles. What the Tathagata speaks of as a union of a single mass is not a union of a single mass; therefore it is called a union of a single mass.
Subhuti, that which is a union of a single mass cannot be spoken of; yet ordinary people are attached to this matter.

blocks.text: Part Thirty-one: The Non-arising of Views

inline.s: Subhuti, if a person says that the Buddha spoke of the view of self, the view of person, the view of being, and the view of lifespan, Subhuti, what do you think? Does that person understand the meaning of what I have spoken? No, World-Honored One, that person does not understand the meaning spoken by the Tathagata. Why? The World-Honored One speaks of the view of self, person, being, and lifespan as not the view of self, person, being, and lifespan; therefore they are called the view of self, person, being, and lifespan.
Subhuti, one who resolves his mind upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi should, with regard to all dharmas, thus know, thus see, thus believe and understand, without giving rise to a mark of dharma.
Subhuti, what are called marks of dharma — the Tathagata speaks of them as not marks of dharma; therefore they are called marks of dharma.
